stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude for Word Beta With AI-Powered Tracked Changes

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude for Word in public beta, bringing AI-powered editing directly into Microsoft Word as a native sidebar add-in for Team and Enterprise users on Mac and Windows.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has officially launched Claude for Word in public beta, bringing its AI assistant directly into Microsoft Word as a native sidebar add-in for Team and Enterprise users on both Mac and Windows platforms.

key_facts.fact: All AI-generated edits surface as Microsoft Word's tracked changes, enabling users to accept or reject each suggestion as they would a human collaborator's markup.
key_facts.excerpt: The integration preserves native document formatting and surfaces all AI-generated edits as Microsoft Word's tracked changes, keeping the revision history intact and fully reviewable by human editors.

key_facts.fact: Claude for Word shares context across Anthropic's Office add-in family — a single conversation thread can span Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents simultaneously.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude for Word connects directly with Claude for Excel and Claude for PowerPoint, meaning a single conversation thread can span all three open documents simultaneously.

key_facts.fact: The add-in can interpret existing Word comment threads and deliver revisions that directly address each note, returning an updated document with tracked changes.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude can also interpret existing comment threads and deliver revisions that directly address each note, returning an updated document with tracked changes showing every edit made.

key_facts.fact: The launch positions Anthropic in direct competition with Microsoft's own 365 Copilot, though early users noted Claude's smoother document-handling and more coherent multi-app context flow.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's own 365 Copilot already offers deep Word integration, but early users of Claude for Word have noted its smoother document-handling and more coherent multi-app context flow as differentiators.

stories.headline: Analysts Say Google's TurboQuant LLM Compression Will Expand, Not Reduce, Memory Demand

key_facts.fact: Google's TurboQuant compression algorithm, detailed in March, can reduce KV cache memory usage by 6x and boost inference speed by 8x for large language models.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant is a compression method that reduces the size of large language models (LLMs) with no loss of accuracy. It achieves this by shrinking the size of memory needed for training LLMs.

key_facts.fact: Despite initial fears that sent memory stocks lower, analysts and researchers now say TurboQuant is more likely to expand memory chip demand than reduce it — by removing bottlenecks, it enables training of bigger, more capable models.
key_facts.excerpt: Even if the technology proves successful in practice and enjoys widespread adoption, it will increase memory demand. Removing a bottleneck, such as huge memory requirements, can help AI companies train bigger, more capable models.

key_facts.fact: LLM parameter counts have grown from 0.09 billion in 2019 to over 1 trillion today; more efficient memory use historically drives demand for larger models rather than reducing total consumption.
key_facts.excerpt: The largest LLM in 2019 had just 0.09 billion parameters, a number that shot up to 540 billion in 2022. Unsurprisingly, the latest LLMs are being trained with more than 1 trillion parameters.

key_facts.fact: FT analysis cites experts concluding that more efficient AI could mean even greater need for semiconductors, reinforcing the Jevons paradox in AI compute.
key_facts.excerpt: More efficient artificial intelligence could mean even greater need for semiconductors, say experts.

key_facts.fact: Memory industry context: DRAM contract prices surged 55-60% QoQ in Q1 2026, with HBM now consuming 23% of total DRAM wafer output, up from 19% the prior year.
key_facts.excerpt: Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 55 to 60% quarter over quarter in Q1, while server DRAM surged more than 60%. HBM now consumes 23% of total DRAM wafer output, up from 19% the prior year.

stories.headline: Linux Kernel Publishes Official AI Coding Guidelines: Humans Must Own Every Line

key_facts.fact: The Linux kernel project published new documentation allowing AI-generated code contributions, provided they comply with existing kernel guidelines, licensing, and attribution requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: The document reveals that people can use AI-generated code, as long as it complies with the guidelines for submitting to the Linux kernel, fits within the license Linux uses, and is attributed to the bot correctly.

key_facts.fact: AI agents are explicitly banned from adding Signed-off-by tags. Only humans can legally certify the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO), and the submitter takes full responsibility for all AI-generated code.
key_facts.excerpt: AI agents MUST NOT add Signed-off-by tags. Only humans can legally certify the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO). The human submitter is responsible for: Reviewing all AI-generated code, Ensuring compliance with licensing requirements, Adding their own Signed-off-by tag to certify the DCO, Taking full responsibility for the contribution.

key_facts.fact: A new 'Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION' attribution tag is required when AI played a meaningful role, creating a disclosure mechanism to track AI-assisted contributions across the kernel.
key_facts.excerpt: Pull requests should use the Assissted-by tag in the following convention: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION [TOOL1] [TOOL2].

key_facts.fact: Linus Torvalds said he doesn't want the documentation to become a 'political battlefield' over AI, noting 'zero point in talking about AI slop' since bad actors who submit garbage AI code won't disclose it anyway.
key_facts.excerpt: His exact take: there's 'zero point in talking about AI slop' in the docs, because bad actors who submit garbage AI code won't disclose it anyway. The guidelines are for good actors.

key_facts.fact: All AI-assisted code must comply with the kernel's existing GPL-2.0-only licensing, use appropriate SPDX license identifiers, and follow the same processes as human-written code.
key_facts.excerpt: All code must comply with the Linux kernel's existing compliance requirements, such as compatibility with GPL-2.0-only, leverage appropriate SPDX license identifiers, and conform to all the rules outlined in license-rules.rst.

stories.headline: OpenAI Discloses North Korean Supply Chain Attack via Compromised Axios Library

key_facts.fact: A GitHub Actions workflow used to sign OpenAI's macOS apps downloaded a malicious version of the Axios JavaScript library on March 31, during a ~3-hour window when the package was compromised.
key_facts.excerpt: A GitHub Actions workflow, an automated process used in software development, downloaded and executed a malicious version of Axios, OpenAI said.

key_facts.fact: The compromised workflow had access to certificate and notarisation material used to sign macOS applications including ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Codex-cli, and Atlas.
key_facts.excerpt: That workflow had access to certificate and notarisation material used to sign macOS applications including ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Codex-cli, and Atlas, the company confirmed.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the signing certificate was likely not successfully extracted by the malicious payload and found no evidence that user data, systems, or IP were compromised.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said its analysis concluded the signing certificate present in the workflow was likely not successfully extracted by the malicious payload.

key_facts.fact: Google's Threat Intelligence Group attributed the Axios npm package compromise to a suspected North Korean threat actor tracked as UNC1069, who hijacked a maintainer's account via AI-enabled social engineering.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's Threat Intelligence Group attributed the attack to a suspected North Korean threat actor it tracks as UNC1069.

key_facts.fact: Axios, one of npm's most widely used HTTP client libraries with ~100 million weekly downloads, was compromised for about three hours after attackers slipped a remote-access trojan into two releases.
key_facts.excerpt: Axios, an open-source JavaScript library that has about 100 million weekly downloads and runs in 80 percent of cloud and code environments.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI attributed the root cause to a misconfiguration in its GitHub Actions workflow, which has since been corrected. All macOS users are required to update to the latest app versions.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI attributed the root cause to a misconfiguration in the GitHub Actions workflow, which it said has since been corrected. As a precautionary measure, the company is updating its security certifications and is requiring all macOS users to update their OpenAI applications.

stories.headline: Ukraine and Russia Swap 175 POWs Each, Begin 32-Hour Orthodox Easter Ceasefire

key_facts.excerpt: Russia's Defence Ministry said the United Arab Emirates had mediated the exchange. Russia took back 175 servicemen and also seven civilians originally from the Kursk region.

key_facts.fact: A 32-hour Easter ceasefire began at 4 p.m. local time (1300 GMT) on Saturday and was set to end at midnight on Sunday, as both countries celebrate Orthodox Easter.

key_facts.fact: 163 of the freed Ukrainians had been held since 2022, marking over four years in captivity. Some had difficulty walking and were transported by ambulance.
key_facts.excerpt: Andrii Yusov, a Ukrainian defence intelligence representative, said 163 of those freed had been held since 2022. "This is a real success, a very significant achievement."

key_facts.fact: US-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia remain stalled over the issue of territory. POW exchanges are among the few concrete results from those negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: They are among the few concrete results to emerge from several rounds of U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, which remain stalled over the issue of territory.

stories.headline: Unitree H1 Humanoid Robot Hits 10 m/s Sprint, Nearing Usain Bolt's Peak Speed

key_facts.fact: On April 11, Unitree Robotics released footage of its H1 humanoid robot reaching a peak running speed of 10 meters per second (22.4 mph), setting a new world record for humanoid robots.
key_facts.excerpt: On April 11, 2026, Unitree Robotics released footage of its H1 model reaching a peak running speed of 10 meters per second (m/s)—approximately 22.4 mph.

key_facts.fact: The H1 weighs approximately 62 kg with a leg length of 0.8 meters; the 10 m/s peak is a 200% increase over its previous record of 3.3 m/s set in early 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Weight: Approximately 62 kg. Leg Length: 0.8 meters. Peak Velocity: 10 m/s. ... this 10 m/s peak represents a 200% increase over the H1's previous record of 3.3 m/s set in early 2024.

key_facts.fact: Usain Bolt's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds translates to a peak speed of 12.42 m/s; the H1's 10 m/s is equivalent to a 10-second 100-meter dash.
key_facts.excerpt: While Bolt's peak speed of 12.42 m/s remains the human benchmark, Unitree's latest demonstration suggests that the 'utility gap' in robotic locomotion is closing faster than many industry analysts expected.

key_facts.fact: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing predicted in March at the Yabuli Forum that humanoids would outrun Bolt by mid-2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 今年3月，宇树科技创始人王兴兴在亚布力论坛上曾说：'今年年中，中国人形机器人百米冲刺将突破10秒大关，超越博尔特。'

key_facts.fact: The H1 is far ahead of competitors: Tesla Optimus recently reached ~2.7 m/s (6 mph) and RobotEra STAR1 demonstrated 3.6 m/s (8 mph).
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla Optimus: Recently reached a personal record of approximately 2.7 m/s (6 mph). RobotEra STAR1: Demonstrated speeds of 3.6 m/s (8.0 mph).

stories.headline: Unitree to Sell R1 Humanoid Robot Globally via AliExpress — First Marketplace Launch

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics will open sales of the R1 humanoid robot outside China via AliExpress next week, making it the first humanoid available for purchase on a general marketplace.
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree Robotics на следующей неделе открывает продажи робота R1 за пределами Китая — через AliExpress, сообщает Gizmochina. Это первый случай, когда гуманоидную машину можно будет заказать онлайн так же, как любой другой товар.

key_facts.fact: Sales will launch in North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore; the R1 is 123 cm tall, weighs 27 kg, and sold in China from 29,900 yuan (~$4,100).
key_facts.excerpt: Старт охватит Северную Америку, Европу, Японию и Сингапур. Сам робот ростом 123 см и массой чуть более 27 кг. В Китае его выпустили в 2025 году по цене от 29 900 юаней.

key_facts.fact: Unitree shipped over 5,500 R1 units in 2025 — more than Tesla, Figure AI, and Agility Robotics combined (each shipped approximately 150 units).
key_facts.excerpt: В 2025 году Unitree отгрузила более 5 500 единиц R1 — больше, чем Tesla, Figure AI и Agility Robotics вместе взятые: каждая из этих компаний поставила примерно по 150 машин.

key_facts.fact: About 70% of R1 orders came from universities and research institutes; the company targets 10,000 to 20,000 units in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Около 70% заказов пришлось на университеты и научные институты. На 2026 год компания ставит цель — от 10 000 до 20 000 единиц.

key_facts.fact: Over 80% of R1 components are manufactured in China, giving Unitree a significant cost advantage over Western competitors whose humanoids cost up to $300,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Более 80% компонентов R1 производят внутри Китая. Для сравнения: аналогичные машины от западных производителей стоят до 300 000 долларов.

sources.title: На маркетплейсе можно будет купить гуманоидного робота Unitree

stories.headline: US Intel: China Preparing to Ship Air Defense Weapons to Iran via Third Countries

key_facts.fact: US intelligence indicates China is preparing to deliver shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems (MANPADs) to Iran within weeks, according to three people familiar with intelligence assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: The systems Beijing is preparing to transfer are shoulder-fired anti-air missile systems known as MANPADs, the sources said, which posed an asymmetric threat to low-flying US military aircraft throughout the course of the five-week war.

key_facts.fact: Beijing is working to route shipments through third countries to mask their origin, two sources said. This would mark an escalation from dual-use technology to direct weapons transfers.
key_facts.excerpt: Two of the sources told CNN there are indications that Beijing is working to route the shipments through third countries to mask their true origin.

key_facts.fact: Trump warned China would face consequences: 'If China does that, China will have big problems, OK?' He is scheduled to visit Beijing next month for talks with Xi Jinping.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked by CNN on Saturday about the US intelligence and whether he has spoken to Xi about the issue, Trump indicated that Beijing would face consequences if it sent weapons to Tehran. "If China does that, China will have big problems, OK?" he said.

key_facts.fact: Chinese Embassy denied the claim: 'China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue.'
key_facts.excerpt: "China has never provided weapons to any party to the conflict; the information in question is untrue," Liu Pengyu, a spokesman for the Chinese diplomatic mission in the United States, told TASS.

key_facts.fact: The intelligence suggests Iran may be using the ceasefire to replenish weapons with help from foreign partners. A US F-15 was shot down over Iran last week reportedly by a 'handheld shoulder missile.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump indicated during a press conference on Monday that the F-15 fighter jet shot down over Iran last week was hit by a 'handheld shoulder missile, [a] heat-seeking missile,' and Tehran said it had used a 'new' air defense system.

sources.title: Exclusive: US intelligence indicates China is preparing weapons shipment to Iran amid fragile ceasefire
China denies plans to supply air defense systems to Iran

stories.headline: US-Iran Islamabad Peace Talks End Without Deal After 21 Hours Over Nuclear Impasse

key_facts.fact: US Vice President JD Vance announced the talks ended without agreement after 21 hours, saying Iran refused to commit to not developing nuclear weapons.
key_facts.excerpt: "The bad news is that we have not reached an agreement... The simple fact is that we need to see an affirmative commitment that they will not seek a nuclear weapon, and they will not seek the tools that would enable them to quickly achieve a nuclear weapon."

key_facts.fact: The talks were the first face-to-face engagement between the US and Iran since 2015, and the highest-level discussions since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: It was the first face-to-face engagement between the U.S. and Iran since 2015, when the Obama administration negotiated a nuclear deal with Iran that was later scrapped by Trump.

key_facts.fact: Iran demanded release of $6 billion in frozen assets, guarantees around its nuclear program, the right to charge ships through the Strait of Hormuz, and an end to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon.
key_facts.excerpt: Other demands from the Iranian delegation included the release of $6 billion in frozen assets, guarantees around its nuclear program and the right to charge ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Vance left a 'final and best offer' on the table, saying 'We'll see if the Iranians accept it,' leaving a narrow path for a future agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: "We leave here with a very simple proposal: a method of understanding that is our final and best offer... We'll see if the Iranians accept it."

key_facts.fact: The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,020 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states since US-Israeli strikes began on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The war has killed at least 3,000 people in Iran, 2,020 in Lebanon, 23 in Israel and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states, and caused lasting damage to infrastructure in half a dozen Middle Eastern countries.

key_facts.fact: Chinese, Egyptian, Saudi and Qatari officials were in Islamabad to indirectly facilitate the talks, reflecting the global stakes of the negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: Reflecting the high stakes, officials from the region said Chinese, Egyptian, Saudi and Qatari officials were in Islamabad to indirectly facilitate the talks.

key_facts.fact: Hours after the talks collapsed, Trump announced a US Navy blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, ordered interdiction of vessels that paid tolls to Iran, and said US forces would destroy Iranian mines.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: US Navy Transits Strait of Hormuz for First Time Since Iran War Began, Starts Mine Clearing

key_facts.fact: Two US Navy guided-missile destroyers passed through the Strait of Hormuz on April 11, the first American warship transit since the Iran war began six weeks ago.
key_facts.excerpt: Minutes before Trump's post, reports started to emerge about the presence of U.S. Navy ships in the strait.

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on Truth Social that the US has started clearing the strait and that 'all 28' of Iran's mine-dropping boats 'are lying at the bottom of the sea.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're now starting the process of clearing out the Strait of Hormuz," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post, adding that "all 28" of Iran's "mine dropper boats are also lying at the bottom of the sea."

key_facts.fact: Iranian state TV denied any US ships had crossed the strait. Iran's military command denied reports about the passage.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's state media, however, earlier said Iran forced a U.S. military ship that was attempting to cross the strait to turn around.

key_facts.fact: The strait's effective closure for ~40 days has disrupted global energy markets and sent oil and gasoline prices soaring, despite most oil flowing through it not going to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Fear of Iranian attacks on shipping over the past several weeks has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a critical conduit for global oil supplies. Throttling the strait has disrupted global energy markets.

key_facts.fact: Three Liberian- and Chinese-flagged supertankers also passed through the strait on Saturday, the first commercial vessels to exit the Gulf since the ceasefire last week.
key_facts.excerpt: Three Liberian- and Chinese-flagged supertankers did pass through the strait today, shipping data showed, marking what appeared to be the first vessels to exit the Gulf since last week's US-Iran ceasefire.
